court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Jxxx vs The District Registrar on 8 October, 2025

parties.respondent_defendant: The District Registrar, Dindigul, Dindigul District; The Sub Registrar, Joint - I Sub - Registrar Office, Dindigul District; Kxxx; The Inspector of Police, Cyber Crime Wing Criminal Branch, Madurai City, Madurai

facts_of_case: Petitioner is an engineering college student who got acquainted with the third respondent. Impugned entry in Marriage Register was registered. Petitioner claims no marriage took place and seeks to quash the same.

legal_principles.principle: The Marriage Registrar may refuse to register the marriage if the application is incomplete, the prescribed fee has not been paid, or any of the conditions prescribed in Sections 5, 6 and 7 of the Act has not been satisfied.
legal_principles.held: Provided that the Marriage Registrar may return the application to the applicant by post for supplying any omission or for rectifying any defect or for clearing any doubt, and for resubmitting the application to the Marriage Registrar within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the application by the applicant with his endorsement thereon.

legal_principles.principle: The Marriage Registrar shall scrutinise the application to ensure it is complete and meets the prescribed conditions.
legal_principles.held: The Marriage Registrar shall, on receipt of the application, scrutinise it or have it scrutinized — (i) the application is incomplete; or (ii) the prescribed fee has not been paid; or (?ii) any of the conditions prescribed in Sections 5, 6 and 7 of the Act has not been satisfied.
applicable_acts_sections: Tamil Nadu Hindu Marriage (Registration) Rules, 1967 — Rule 8

use_for_drafting: drafting a writ petition for quashing a marriage registration
advising on the validity of a marriage registration
representing a client in a case involving fraud, coercion, or misrepresentation
